verdicts.corrected_claim: The limit exists (10 per 60 s per IP per route on every /auth/ path, shared NAT hits it). But a check-email 429 is swallowed and blocks nothing, so typing bursts do not show an error; the 429 matters for register/login routes. House opening shows specific 'Too many tries' copy; account register shows only err.message. Also the key trusts the first x-forwarded-for entry, so it is client-spoofable. Still inferred, not observed.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The maybeSingle-errors-for-multi-house part is wrong: user_id is UNIQUE, so at most one row. The real defect is that one row per user points at one house, so a multi-house person reads one house's progress. Confirmed: GET writes (self-heal), heal matches status='active' only so an onboarding draft never heals, read errors swallowed, heal uses the row's restaurant_id, client can PATCH any flag true. Wrong: PATCH progress has NO tenant match (user_id only), so no cross-tenant write, and no role check.

Wrong: currency is not silent (shown on the page); the name is prefilled from the account, so it is re-confirmed not re-typed.

verdicts.corrected_claim: Non-transactional chain confirmed (about 6 server stages plus the client /auth/me). But it already compensates: the catch deletes restaurant and org, users.restaurant_id is ON DELETE SET NULL and the onboarding row cascades, so a caught failure retries clean rather than 409. An unreachable org or a 409 needs the compensating deletes themselves to fail (their errors are not checked) or the process to die.
